title: Anchor the test-directory glob so the sweep stops reading history dirs
action: The pg-4 goal-check judge raised one non-blocking advisory it proved by running the command: `fd -t d tests` in row 6 of the Provenance sweep matches any directory whose BASENAME contains 'tests', so it also returns docs/history/scripts-tests-move/ and docs/history/workflow-verb-tests/ — the sweep reads two history directories as test directories. In skills/bee-researching/references/trace-and-provenance.md, row 6 only, anchor the pattern so it matches a directory actually named tests. Change nothing else in the file. Then run the regen chain in order: bee dev render-skill-trees, then bee onboard --repo-root . --apply, then bee dev release-manifest --write.
verify: The anchored command run in this repo returns only directories named exactly tests, and returns real hits against a known behavior term. bee dev release-manifest --check is clean and the rendered copies match the source.

trace.outcome: The provenance sweep's test-directory glob is anchored, so it returns only directories named tests

report.outcome: The provenance sweep test-directory glob is anchored, so it returns only directories named tests
report.tests: fd -t d anchored then rg over its three results, plus bee dev release-manifest --check — green:live — docs cell: the anchored glob returned only expertise/tests, crates/bee/tests and crates/fleet/tests, the rg over them returned real hits, and the five rendered copies are byte-identical to the source

checks.evidence: fd -t d '^tests$' in this repo returns exactly expertise/tests/, packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/ and packages/bee-rs/crates/fleet/tests/. The old unanchored pattern also returned docs/history/scripts-tests-move/ and docs/history/workflow-verb-tests/; both are gone.

bash -c with the row-6 command over a real term printed 39 hits, e.g. packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/concurrency.rs:579 and tests/session_release.rs:5, rg exit 0. The unquoted substitution word-splits correctly under a plain bash -c, checked both inline and by running the row's verbatim text.

git show 739852bc --stat: 13 files, 17 insertions / 17 deletions. The source diff is the single row-6 line. The other twelve are the five rendered copies (same one line), five .bee-render.json hash files, .bee/onboarding.json and the release manifest, whose diffs carry only sha256 values and one timestamp. md5sum on the source and all five copies is 230b202fdf6eea5c27172aec1490bf8c, and bee dev release-manifest --check reports 295 files matching, exit 0.

fd 10.4.2 at /usr/bin/fd treats the pattern as a regex by default and matches the base name. Proved by differential test rather than by docs: fd -t d --glob '^tests$' returns 0 results (glob mode reads the anchors literally), fd -t d '^tests$' returns 3, fd -t d '^test$' returns 0, and fd -t d '^tests?$' returns 3.
